validator_run.raw_output: raw exit 0 on the integrated SHA; go test ./... = 0 with 35 packages

review_notes.round_1: REJECT. The xss pattern flagged innerHTML = DOMPurify.sanitize(userInput) -- the recommended mitigation -- because it required the right-hand side to START with an identifier without requiring it to END there. Reproduced against the candidate's own compiled binary.
review_notes.round_2: APPROVE of the rule. Calls are now excluded uniformly, and the reviewer confirmed the positive control survived whole: all six dangerous shapes still fall. They tried and failed to find a conventional JavaScript name for user data starting with an uppercase letter, which validates the builder's argument for excluding PascalCase and SCREAMING_SNAKE.
review_notes.round_3: APPROVE of the harness rewrite. The acceptance had to lose git and python3, which the sealed image lacks. The reviewer diffed the 146 lines removed from the integration program and confirmed only the git init factory left, no assertion; re-ran the awk mutations outside the script and compared the produced content, confirming both hit their intended target rather than silently missing and leaving a green gate.
review_notes.declared_costs: Written in docs/specs/AUR-462.md: innerHTML = getUserInput() is no longer caught, because shape alone cannot separate a sanitiser call from a dangerous one; and an uppercase-initial identifier is excluded by convention.
review_notes.measured_effect: On the five-defect JavaScript fixture the pass now finds five of five, against three before: exec( and innerHTML were invisible. The coverage line moved from 3 of 8 to 4 of 8.
